newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Independent's W&H bid may cost up to 442 mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Independent's W&H bid may cost up to 442 mln punts.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Plc said on Monday that if its subsidiary's offer for New Zealand publisher Wilson and Horton was fully taken up, it would cost NZ$1.03 billion or 442 million Irish pounds.

A new 400 million punt borrowing facility has been made available to finance the acquisition, to refinance certain existing borrowings of Wilson and Horton and Independent Newspapers and to provide working capital.
If the offer is fully accepted and a share alternative fully taken up, group net debt would rise to 370 million punts from 164 million at December 1995, Independent said in a statement.
The acquisition should have a marginally beneficial effect on earnings per share in the short term and should deliver significant benefits thereafter, the company said.
The successful acquisition of Wilson and Horton, owner of the New Zealand Herald, should also help propel group profits before interest and tax above 100 million punts, it said.

"The important thing for us is that it propels us into the 100 million plus category in PBIT terms," a company spokesman told Reuters. "It propels us into being a very strong international media company."
Independent's brokers, Davy Stockbrokers, have just revised their 1996 pre-tax profit forecasts for the group upward.

Following the release last week of half-year results showing a 28 percent rise in pre-tax profits, they are now predicting full-year pre-tax profits of 65 million Irish pounds, up from 61 million previously.
Brokers expect Wilson and Horton to report profits of around 40 million punts this year, the Independent spokesman said.
The surprise takeover bid for Wilson and Horton was announced earlier on Monday by Independent Press Communications Ltd (IPCL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Independent Newspapers.
IPCL said it intended to offer NZ$10.50/share to purchase all outstanding shares of Wilson and Horton.
The offer included a partial share alternative of up to NZ$320 of IPCL preference shares.
Wilson and Horton issued a notice advising shareholders not to sell for the time being and analysts said the offer might not be enough to take over such a strong franchise.

But the Independent spokesman noted that expectations of an offer had already been partly built into the Wilson and Horton share price which has been around $9.50 for some time but closed at $9.70 on Monday.

Dublin analysts also said the prospect of the emergence of a a counterbidder seemed remote given that Independent and family trusts linked to its chairman Tony O'Reilly hold 45.15 percent of Wilson and Horton.
Independent's share price was unchanged in Dublin at 295.25 by 1100 GMT.
